subject: research/capture-softgate

evidence.verification: /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests: 7 passed. Seven seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py in hybrid.py: five SURVIVED - match_cost max -> min (the cost signal under test takes the best source instead of the worst), disagreement masked by o1|o2 instead of o1&o2, row_fill picking the nearer instead of the farther neighbour (foreground fill), the output blend inverted (w*base + (1-w)*nearest: every gate does the opposite of its definition), and softcost np.maximum -> np.minimum. Two were caught (ramp denominator, oracle comparison reversed). Tests check weight ranges and edge cases, never that a gate improves on plain synthesis or that the blend direction is right; experiments/run.py (edge_excess, parameter selection, the hard-gate tau wrapper) has no test, and no test pins any number in results.txt.
evidence.craft: Read src/capture_softgate/hybrid.py, scene.py, stereo.py, synth.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, tests/test_softgate.py. Small, vectorised, readable numpy with docstrings. Defects: scene/stereo/synth are copied engine files from capture-hybrid (itself copied from capture-stereodepth) rather than a shared package; the hard gate reuses the soft gate's t0 parameter as its tau (hybrid.py:98, run.py:83-85 wrapper re-runs avg just to swap it), an easy-to-misuse API; make()'s default ct=0.4 (hybrid.py:111) differs from the chosen 0.1; synth.synthesise and stereo.depth_errors are unused here. No silent fallbacks or unhandled-input issues for a research script.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'soft ahead of hard in all 11 rows, by 0.1 to 0.5 dB' (11/11, 0.07-0.45); held-out 29.3 -> 29.5 and 26.5 -> 26.7; 'closes about 0.25 dB of the 2.6 dB gap ... about a tenth' (0.096); cost 27.6 vs fill 27.3, 24.5 vs 26.2, 24.1 vs 25.8; seam numbers as printed; 7 tests; parameter selection on dev seeds and the larger soft sweep are disclosed honestly. Not backed: the headline 'cuts false edges (seams) by about a quarter' (README:3, :43). The seam score (run.py:41-46) is mean gradient magnitude minus the truth's, which rewards blur and noise averaging: independently (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/51f1effa-64ec-5629-99d4-286a0580a520/scratchpad/capture/blur.py) a 3x3-blurred truth scores -0.028 ('better than the truth'), and averaging two 1%-noise copies drops a copy's 0.0056 to 0.0036 - the same scale as the claimed hard 0.0087 -> soft 0.0067 effect, and soft blends two noisy sources. In the subject's own table soft (0.0067) beats the ground-truth-chosen oracle (0.0072), which a seam measure should not allow. Under a gradient-error metric |grad(out)-grad(truth)| on the subject's held-out outputs (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/51f1effa-64ec-5629-99d4-286a0580a520/scratchpad/capture/probe.py) hard -> soft is 0.0376 -> 0.0367 (2.4%) and 0.0407 -> 0.0394 (3.2%) with a bystander, where soft is worse than plain fill (0.0388). The Limitations do say 'a global gradient statistic, not a seam detector', but the headline still says seams by a quarter. 'The stereo matching cost is a worse confidence signal than the disagreement' (README:3) generalises from raw window cost only. Minor: 'gate family only 0.3 to 0.5 dB above filling with a bystander' (README:44) - soft at gap 8 is 0.72 above; 'about 2 minutes' (README:25) vs 18 s.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can run and extend it in minutes; the result reproduces on an independent second scene, so the soft > hard ordering is sound for this toy setting. Nearest prior work: per-pixel continuous blending weights for view-synthesis sources are the core of Unstructured Lumigraph Rendering (Buehler et al., SIGGRAPH 2001) and view-dependent texture mapping (Debevec et al. 1996); soft visibility/confidence for view synthesis is Penner & Zhang, 'Soft 3D Reconstruction for View Synthesis' (SIGGRAPH Asia 2017); learned per-pixel blend weights (the project's own next step) are Hedman et al., 'Deep Blending for Free-Viewpoint IBR' (SIGGRAPH Asia 2018); seam suppression at depth boundaries is Zitnick et al. 2004 (boundary matting). That raw matching cost (MSM) is a weak stereo confidence and left-right consistency / peak-ratio measures are better is the main finding of Hu & Mordohai, 'A Quantitative Evaluation of Confidence Measures for Stereo Vision' (TPAMI 34(11), 2012). None is cited; the README says only that soft blending 'is standard'. The cost result therefore re-finds a known result with the weakest measure, and capture-hybrid's next step asked for the left-right mask and cost margin, which were not tried. A correct, honest incremental notebook step (0.25 dB on one toy scene), not a new result at the PhD/publishable bar of research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Mechanics match standard DIBR practice: forward z-buffer splatting, crack closing, background-side disocclusion fill, PSNR against an exact ray-traced target, frozen parameters with held-out seeds, oracle upper bound. A senior IBR/stereo researcher would not sign off on two points: (1) the seam metric is unvalidated and confounded with blur/noise (see claims); a gradient-similarity measure (e.g. GMSD, Xue et al. 2014), an edge-localised measure along the weight transitions, or SSIM would be expected; (2) the confidence comparison omits the standard measures (LRC, PKRN / peak ratio, cost curvature; Hu & Mordohai 2012) and uses one global threshold. Also: 3 noise seeds on one deterministic scene, no per-seed spread or paired test for 0.07-0.25 dB differences (9 of the 11 conditions use the tuning seeds; disclosed).

defects.what: The headline 'cuts false edges (seams) by about a quarter' rests on a seam score (mean gradient magnitude minus the truth's) that rewards blur and noise averaging: a 3x3-blurred truth scores -0.028, averaging two 1%-noise copies lowers the score by 0.002 (the size of the claimed effect), and soft scores better than the ground-truth oracle. Under a gradient-error metric the hard->soft reduction is 2.4% (3.2% with a bystander, where soft is worse than plain fill).

Core logic untested: 5 of 7 seeded mutants survive, including the output blend inverted (every gate does the opposite of its definition), match_cost max->min, the disagreement mask widened to either-valid, foreground instead of background hole fill, and softcost max->min. No test asserts a gate improves on plain synthesis or pins a results.txt number; run.py (edge_excess, selection) is untested.

No prior work cited: continuous per-pixel blending of view-synthesis sources (Buehler et al. 2001 Unstructured Lumigraph; Penner & Zhang 2017; Hedman et al. 2018 Deep Blending) and the finding that raw matching cost is a weak stereo confidence while LRC / peak-ratio measures are better (Hu & Mordohai, TPAMI 2012). The general claim 'stereo matching cost is a worse confidence signal' is tested only with raw window cost, not the LR mask or cost margin capture-hybrid's next step asked for. Below the research/CLAUDE.md publishable bar on novelty.

Hard gate reuses the soft gate's t0 as its threshold tau (run.py needs a wrapper that re-runs avg to swap it in), and make()'s default ct=0.4 differs from the chosen 0.1; scene/stereo/synth are copied engines from capture-hybrid.
'gate family only 0.3 to 0.5 dB above plain filling' with a bystander: soft at an 8 degree gap is 0.72 dB above (results.txt D).
Reproduce says run.py takes 'about 2 minutes'; it ran in 18 s.

verdict: capture-softgate's numbers are right: run.py reproduces results.txt byte-for-byte, the figure regenerates identically, and an independent re-implementation on a different toy scene reproduces the ordering (soft > hard in 5/5 held-out conditions by 0.08-0.30 dB; cost gate level with fill and about 1.8 dB below it with a bystander or noise). The hard baseline is fairly tuned (extending its sweep finds no better tau). It misses the bar on verification and claims: 5 of 7 seeded bugs survive the 7 tests, including an inverted output blend, and the headline 'about a quarter fewer seams' comes from a gradient-excess score that rewards blur and noise averaging (soft even beats the ground-truth oracle on it); under a gradient-error metric the gain is about 3%. As research it is an honest, incremental step (0.25 of 2.6 dB on one scene) that cites none of the IBR blending or stereo-confidence literature and re-finds Hu & Mordohai's (2012) result with the weakest confidence measure; not publishable-grade.
